tasks.short: Compile order statistics and prepare management reports.

steps.what: Export orders, cancellations and order values for the reporting period.
Retrieve shipment dates and outstanding quantities.
Match exports, resolve discrepancies and calculate agreed order statistics.
Prepare the management report and explain material changes.
Email the report to management and retain the distributed version.

tasks.design: Scheduled exports from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} feed deterministic joins, reconciliations and calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. An artefact generator prepares tables and threshold-based variance statements; the order clerk resolves exceptions and adds explanations before publishing an approved snapshot in the {BI}. Management reads the shared snapshot, removing attachment distribution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate exports, inconsistent order identifiers and changing metric definitions make a recurring report costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and reporting features can cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building missing joins, checks and report templates; no model is needed at runtime.
tasks.still_hard: Partial deliveries, returns, currency changes and reporting cut-offs can change the meaning of a metric. Explaining causes still needs operational knowledge.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparent sales change is a data issue, and explain which operational action management should consider.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of overdue order exceptions instead of waiting for the management reporting cycle.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to investigating exceptions and proposing order-recovery priorities. Commercial and fulfilment approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare an evidence-based order-recovery priority list.
reach.learn: Backlog ageing, margin interpretation and the limits of order-value measures.

evidence.claim: Fixed order metrics, reconciliation checks and report templates can use deterministic calculations.
Exact documents order imports and stock synchronisation, supporting the feasibility of connected order records.

assumptions: This typical workflow uses separate order and shipment records, with a spreadsheet joining them.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Existing reporting configuration is checked before custom code is built.
Access is limited to necessary order data under GDPR; national consultation rules apply if employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Whether the existing {ERP} already provides the required report.
Availability of stable order identifiers and scheduled exports.
Agreed definitions for cancellations, returns, overdue orders and reporting cut-offs.
Who may publish management figures and access customer-level detail.
research_questions: Which reconciliation checks detect duplicate lines and missing shipments?
Can an approved shared snapshot satisfy management's reporting needs?
new_work: Review reconciliation exceptions and unexplained changes.
Maintain metric definitions, reporting calendars and access permissions.
Monitor failed refreshes and preserve approved report versions.

tasks.short: Recommend suitable packing and labels for customer orders.

steps.what: Check ordered items, quantities, destination and recorded handling requirements.
Read customer packing instructions and applicable packing specifications.

loop.input: Customer instructions and the current packing specifications.
loop.output: Structured packing requirements with source passages and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Validate required fields, units and document versions; the clerk confirms extracted requirements before use.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per instruction pack; unresolved or missing requirements go to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer instructions contain varied prose, exceptions and document layouts that fixed field mappings cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Select a packing method and label specification against the requirements.
Resolve nonstandard requirements and approve exceptional packing arrangements.
Record packing and label instructions on the order for fulfilment.

tasks.design: The {ERP} supplies item and destination attributes, while a bounded extraction loop turns instructions in the {DOCS} into requirements for clerk review. Versioned rules in the {WORKFLOW} select standard packing and labels; unmatched or conflicting requirements go to the warehouse supervisor. Only rule-covered recommendations or approved exception plans become packing instructions in the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Packing knowledge is split between specifications, customer instructions and warehouse experience. Incomplete item attributes prevent reliable rule matching.
tasks.enabler_now: A small extraction loop can prepare free-text requirements, while ordinary rules handle known combinations. Existing order fields and approval configuration can carry the result.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition, unusual loads and safety-critical shipments need qualified judgement. Extraction cannot establish that a packing method is safe or legally sufficient.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unusual handling risks, question conflicting instructions and involve qualified specialists when needed.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching specifications and retyping instructions, and more time resolving unusual requirements with fulfilment staff. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Clarify customer handling requirements before an order is accepted.
reach.learn: Packing constraints, label requirements and when to seek warehouse or specialist advice.

evidence.claim: Standard packing choices can use versioned decision tables when item and shipment attributes are complete.
Rossum documents extraction from order documents, business-rule checks and exception routing; this supports the capture pattern, not packing safety.

assumptions: The workflow covers ordinary merchandise; specialist shipments are routed to qualified people.
Approved packing rules exist or can be documented before automated selection starts.
Time shares are averaged across routine orders and orders requiring consultation.
Build ranges include access approval and a national consultation check; they exclude developing specialist packing standards.
Customer documents receive purpose-limited access and retention under GDPR.
unknowns: Completeness of item dimensions, weights and handling classifications.
Which packing standards and destination requirements apply.
Who is qualified to approve safety-critical or nonstandard arrangements.
Whether the {ERP} can enforce unresolved-exception holds.
research_questions: Which requirements can be expressed as complete, testable rules?
What test set covers conflicting instructions, missing attributes and obsolete specifications?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve ambiguous passages.
Maintain packing rules, specification versions and specialist escalation routes.
Investigate incorrect recommendations and update the regression examples.

tasks.short: Sell relevant additional merchandise or services through calls and customer visits.

steps.what: Review account history, recent orders and open customer issues.
Check product information and select relevant additional offers.
Discuss needs, propose useful additions and respond to objections by phone.
Record the conversation outcome and schedule agreed follow-up.

loop.input: Clerk-written conversation notes and the permitted customer-record fields.
loop.output: Draft opportunity fields and follow-up actions with supporting note passages.
loop.check: Validate field types and dates; the clerk confirms intent, commitments and actions before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per conversation; unclear commitments remain blank for clerk completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes describe needs and commitments in varied language; fixed rules cannot reliably map them to fields.

steps.what: Approve proposed discounts or commitments outside the clerk's delegated authority.
Send the agreed offer or follow-up information to the customer.

tasks.design: The {CRM} assembles an account brief, and deterministic compatibility and eligibility rules produce an offer shortlist from approved information in the {DOCS}. The clerk conducts the conversation; a bounded loop converts their notes into reviewed {CRM} updates and follow-up tasks. An artefact generator prepares the customer offer in the {EMAIL}, with approval required for exceptional terms and for sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Account preparation and follow-up span separate records, while customer conversations resist scripting. Reliable records still depend on the clerk completing paperwork.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured account views and small generators reduce preparation effort. A bounded extraction loop can turn the clerk's notes into editable records without recording calls.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, timing, objections and commercial judgement remain human work. Poor product compatibility data can make an apparently relevant suggestion unsuitable.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the customer's situation, recognise when selling would be unhelpful and negotiate within delegated authority.

ambition.what: Small repeat accounts receiving a scheduled replenishment call.

tasks.altitude: Preparation and paperwork shrink, leaving more time for useful customer conversations and planned follow-up. The clerk can prioritise eligible accounts within an agreed contact policy; pricing authority stays unchanged.

reach.task: Develop a qualified additional-sales opportunity from a replenishment conversation.
reach.learn: Needs discovery, product compatibility, qualification and commercial boundaries.

reach.task: Summarise recurring objections for a proposed offer change.
reach.learn: Distinguish repeated evidence from isolated comments and assess margin implications.

evidence.claim: Account briefs, rule-based offer shortlists and template offers can reduce administrative work without automating the sales conversation.
The NBER study reports productivity gains from assistance in customer support; it does not establish additional-sales conversion gains.
GDPR Article 22 restricts certain solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.

assumptions: The representative workflow uses phone calls; customer visits retain the same human conversation step.
The {CRM} exposes account history and customer issues sufficiently for an account brief.
Follow-up offers use standard templates, with explicit approval of exceptional terms.
No call recording or employee scoring is introduced; consultation obligations are checked under national rules.
GDPR and applicable national marketing rules govern contact selection, customer data and retention.
Time shares include averaged exception-approval effort; build ranges are estimates.
unknowns: Which accounts may be contacted and where objections or contact permissions are recorded.
Quality of product compatibility, eligibility and current offer information.
The clerk's delegated pricing and commitment limits.
Whether national rules or collective arrangements require employee consultation.
research_questions: Which offer rules can exclude unsuitable suggestions before a conversation?
Does reduced preparation time enable useful replenishment calls without increasing unwanted contact?
Can note extraction preserve uncertainty without inventing customer commitments?
new_work: Confirm extracted outcomes and follow-up dates.
Maintain offer eligibility, compatibility rules and contact exclusions.
Handle missing account history and outdated product information.
Review customer response and stop contact patterns that prove unhelpful.

role.altitude: The order clerk spends less time joining exports, searching instructions and updating records. More of the week goes to order exceptions, fulfilment coordination and customer conversations; additional commercial authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Support sales managers with order-recovery priorities.
Help sales representatives clarify handling needs before order acceptance.
Develop qualified opportunities from repeat-customer conversations.
skills_to_grow: Customer needs discovery and commercial qualification.
Checking extracted requirements and customer commitments.
role.ambitious_version: An order clerk who combines reliable order intelligence with practical customer support: spotting recoverable delays, resolving handling questions early and developing relevant repeat-account opportunities.
